title: POC Weekly Sync: Quantization INT8/FP8 - Week 10
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quantization experiments across INT8 and FP8. Reviewed quality regressions on rouge/EM-style evals, perf deltas (latency and throughput), and infra concerns for Dedicated vs Private testing. Agreed next steps: run 48-hour INT8 mixed-batch run, collect eval set with user prompts, Priya to provision additional VPC test nodes, Jordan to share updated perf spreadsheet and recommended config by EOD 2026-12-24.
action_items: Jordan: Share updated perf spreadsheet (latency, tokens/sec, cost delta) and suggested config for production pilot - due 2026-12-24
Priya N: Provision 3 additional VPC test nodes for private run and enable KMS test key - due 2026-12-23
Carlos: Expand eval prompt set with 500 user-simulated queries and label edge cases -> upload to shared drive - due 2026-12-27
Samir: Run infra smoke test on quantized FP8 build and report GPU memory behavior - due 2026-12-24
next_steps: Run 48h INT8 mixed-batch run in Private env (Priya + Samir)
Collect baseline metrics for INT8/FP8: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, perf/cost ratio
Jordan to schedule perf deep-dive next Tuesday with broader infra team
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SRE) -- Carlos Martinez (NovaSearch ML), Priya Singh (NovaSearch Infra), Aisha Khan (NovaSearch CTO)

Summary: quick weekly check-in on quantization experiments. We went over results from last week's INT8 run and the new FP8 baseline, talked about quality delta on our rouge-style and instruction-following prompts, and flagged infra issues seen in the private deployment.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this tight, got about 45 minutes. Priya and Samir from our side, and Carlos, Priya S., Aisha from NovaSearch, hi.
[00:12] Carlos: Hey, thanks, yeah, quick note - we kicked off the INT8 run last Monday and got about 36 hours of data, then paused for the FP8 build.
[00:20] Priya N: Great, Carlos, did you run the same batch sizes and seq lengths for both?
[00:25] Carlos: Mostly yes, there was one difference, we had to lower batch size by 1 for the FP8 because of oom on one node, so not perfectly apples-to-apples.
[00:34] Samir: Right, on the FP8 nodes we saw the peaky memory behavior which I think is due to the kernel selection on that driver stack, probably the fused attention kernel isn't stable.
[00:42] Priya S: That's what I was worried about, we haven't tuned the kernel flags on the private env, it's stock.
[00:47] Jordan: Ok noted. Quick go-through of top-level numbers we pulled - INT8 gave ~1.8x token/sec on average vs baseline FP32, p99 latency up ~20ms, and quality drop was small on the instrumental tasks but visible on a subset of instruction-following queries.
[01:05] Carlos: When you say small, can you quantify? Our internal eval shows around 1.8% drop on the rouge-like metric and some hallucination increase on long-hops.
[01:14] Priya N: That matches our eval. For INT8 the EM-style pass rate dropped 2-3% on the thin-tail examples, FP8 is closer to baseline but with more infra instability.
[01:23] Aisha: For us the business question is whether that 2-3% is acceptable for the search summarization flows - if it affects business metrics we're not comfortable.
[01:30] Jordan: Totally get it. That's why we recommended running the INT8 with mixed-batch (some higher precision for critical requests) and keep FP8 as a candidate if we can stabilize the kernel.
[01:40] Carlos: We also noticed tokenizer mismatches in a few corner cases - might be preproc differences between our pipeline and Redwood's docker.
[01:47] Samir: We'll add a quick preproc checksum script to ensure tokenization parity, that'll help verify the evaluation delta is due to quantization not tokenization.
[01:55] Priya S: On infra - we need to run the FP8 build in the dedicated private nodes with the newer NCCL and driver stack. I can spin up nodes but need guidance on the specific kernel flags from Redwood.
[02:06] Priya N: We'll send the recommended kernel flags and a docker diff. Also, Priya S, you'll want the KMS test key for encrypted model shards?
[02:13] Priya S: Yes please. Encryption at rest is a hard requirement for us.
[02:17] Jordan: Action: Priya N will provide the kernel flags and docker diff. Samir will share the FP8 smoke script.
[02:23] Carlos: Can we talk cost numbers? INT8 in our model cuts GPU hours by roughly 35% in your spreadsheet, is that accurate?
[02:31] Jordan: Our spreadsheet shows token-level cost down by ~32% for INT8 at current batch profiles, FP8 shows similar cost reduction but you pay more ops overhead if you have to patch kernels. The spreadsheet will have the exact per-100k token math.
[02:44] Aisha: What's the operational risk? If FP8 leads to random OOMs we could see outages.
[02:50] Samir: The risk is real - we observed an OOM during a spike in one FP8 run, likely due to reduced headroom from fused kernels and unexpected allocation patterns. We recommend a canary rollout with auto-fallback to FP32 or INT8.
[03:03] Jordan: We have routing policies that can fallback automatically; we can set a p95/p99 SLO spike threshold to route to INT8 or FP32 on failure.
[03:11] Carlos: For evals, we added 200 more user prompts focusing on multi-step reasoning. Early look shows FP8 recovers some of the INT8 regressions on those prompts, but again infra noise.
[03:23] Priya N: Interesting. So FP8 quality is closer to FP32 on those reasoning prompts, which tracks with what we've seen in lab experiments. The tradeoff is stability.
[03:31] Priya S: If we can't stabilize FP8 in private, can we test on Dedicated first?
[03:36] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated is a good middle ground - lower infra variability than private and still isolated per-customer. We can spin up a short Dedicated window for a 48-hour run if you want.
[03:45] Aisha: Cost implications?
[03:47] Jordan: Short Dedicated testing is doable; cost will be higher than private at scale but lower than a full production Dedicated commit. We'll include expected cost in the spreadsheet.
[03:56] Carlos: About metrics, can we get per-prompt breakdowns and examples of failure modes? Screenshots or raw logs would help the ML team triage.
[04:03] Priya N: We'll export per-prompt diffs and attach a CSV with example pairs. Also we'll mark edge cases where tokenization mismatch occurs.
[04:10] Carlos: Perfect.
[04:13] Jordan: Quick sanity check on evaluation quality thresholds: Aisha - do you have a hard cutoff for rouge-style or is it more of a business-impact discussion?
[04:21] Aisha: There's no single number but a soft threshold: under 1% regression is ideal, 1-2% acceptable with cost offsets, anything >2% needs careful review.
[04:31] Jordan: Great, so current INT8 1.8% sits in that acceptable band but we want to tighten testing on the 2-3% tail.
[04:39] Priya S: Also want to note SSO/SAML and audit logs - if we run private tests we'll need audit log capture for model start/stop and KMS access events.
[04:48] Jordan: Redwood supports audit logs and KMS integrations; we'll share the security pack.
[04:52] Carlos: Any blockers for the next run?
[04:55] Samir: I need to validate the FP8 docker build on one node, run the smoke test, and share results. That should be done by Thursday.
[05:03] Jordan: Ok let's recap and call out owners.

-- Recap / Next steps --
[05:10] Jordan: Priya N -> send kernel flags + docker diff; Samir -> FP8 smoke script and run; Priya S -> provision 3 VPC test nodes + KMS test key; Carlos -> expand eval set and upload; Jordan -> share perf spreadsheet and recommended config. Aim to run 48h INT8 mixed-batch in private starting Monday, or Dedicated if private instability persists.
[05:32] Aisha: Sounds good, we want a short sync after the 48h run to decide rollout strategy.
[05:37] Jordan: We'll schedule that. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: there are a few places where names got combined (Priya / Priya S) and a couple of words were garbled - e.g., 'fused' heard as 'fuse', 'OOM' sometimes expanded as 'oh-em-oh'.

Links / Artifacts referenced: perf spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.share/perf/novasearch-quant-2026-12-22), FP8 docker diff (link: internal), security pack (link: https://redwood.share/security/redwood-security-pack.pdf)

End of transcript.
